format: Serialized comic released page-by-page and compiled into issues/collections
premise: Actual 9th-century Vikings displaced into contemporary New York become the responsibility of the underfunded NYC Department of Temporal Integration and must build a life inside modern civic systems without being reduced to something easier to process.
emotionalCore: What it means to become responsible for people who did not ask for your help and will not stop needing it.

worldRules.timeSlips: Legally recognized anomalies with established municipal procedures for temporal migrants. The physics are not the dramatic focus.
worldRules.dti: Department of Temporal Integration is an underfunded NYC municipal social-services-style bureaucracy. Its power is paperwork, deadlines, eligibility, status, inspection, and reviewable decisions rather than advanced technology.
worldRules.dtiNaming: DTI is the official production name. In-world signs/forms may intentionally use subtly inconsistent municipal variants.
worldRules.documentary: Documentary/mockumentary language is production style only. Characters do not see or acknowledge a documentary crew.
worldRules.newYork: Locals generally do not stop in amazement at Vikings; ordinary New York indifference is part of the series behavior.

storyEngine: Modern systems collide with Viking logic. Housing, transit, banking, reputation, libraries, work, identity systems, bureaucracy, medicine, courts, and residency are interpreted through territory, passage, tolls, treaties, hoards, assemblies, status, tribute, trial, command, obligation, and survival. The old framework may be wrong in form while perceptive about power, dignity, fear, work, care, or responsibility.

tone.rule: The premise is absurd; the characters do not behave as though they are in an absurd story.
tone.vikings: Heavy stillness, ritual gravity, physical economy, intelligence, dignity, no winking at the premise.
tone.carrie: Fast, sarcastic, exhausted, warm, administratively capable, increasingly protective.
tone.institutions: Pressure comes from rational procedure, scarcity, and mismatched systems more often than individual malice.

comedyGrammar: Ancient functional interpretation of modern objects and systems
New York indifference to Bjorn's ceremonial intensity
Modern euphemisms stripped bare by Viking vocabulary
Carrie's bureaucratic combat through forms, deadlines, wording, and policy
Gunnar's apparently wrong interpretation proving structurally useful
The Vikings noticing genuine modern miracles such as libraries, hot water, medicine, surgery, longevity, and expanded rights
guardrails: Do not make the Vikings stupid to land jokes.
Do not turn DTI into a glamorous federal or science-fiction agency.
Do not use a visible/acknowledged documentary crew as story lore.
Do not use Atavistic Projection as canon.
Do not use Functional Congruence as named canon terminology or an in-world mechanism.
Do not reduce Carrie to an annoyed caretaker.
Do not reduce Gunnar to Bjorn's sidekick.
Do not lock Silas as a pure antagonist.
Do not lock Magister as a simple recurring villain.
Do not make New York locals act amazed by Vikings.

visualProduction.overall: Bright, ordinary 2026 documentary-sitcom realism with tactile material specificity.
visualProduction.dti: Fluorescent, toner-gray, stale coffee, laminate, institutional fatigue.
visualProduction.civicSpaces: Harsh public lighting, scratched glass, plastic seating, linoleum, laminated signage.
visualProduction.materialRule: Forms have colors; keys are brass; walls are drywall; counters are laminate; machines and objects should feel tactile and specific.
visualProduction.paletteGuardrail: Avoid generic beige/tan/sepia/muddy neutral drift unless specifically justified by released canon.

authority: Canonical teleplay and approved production scripts
workingRule: Before inventing connective tissue for an existing sequence, inspect the relevant teleplay/scene inventory. Once a creative decision is approved, encode it into active reference data rather than preserving permanent clarification artifacts.
